sources.title: Gabriel Navarro / Joan Martínez course notes, Representation Theory of Finite Groups
sources.locator: Lecture 3, printed pp. 15–20, and Lecture 4, printed pp. 23–28; especially Definition 4.2, Lemma 4.4, Theorems 4.5 and 4.10.
sources.reading_status: The complete listed passages were fetched and inspected, including the central-character construction, Brauer-map localization, defect containment, and all three parts of the First Main Theorem proof.

contents.name: Definition 4.2, induced block via central characters
contents.support: Supports the traditional central-character formulation compared with the primary bimodule definition.

contents.name: Lemma 4.4, defect containment under block induction
contents.support: Independent central-character treatment of the controlled-defect conclusion.

contents.name: Theorem 4.5, existence and Brauer-map formula
contents.support: Supports the restricted H≤N_G(D) central-character/Brauer-map clause.

contents.name: Corollary 4.6, blocks occurring in Br_D(e_B)
contents.support: Used as an independent check on the local-block selection; the manifest proves existence by the complete Green route.

contents.name: Theorem 4.9, class localization
contents.reason: The required localization machinery belongs to the existing Brauer-homomorphism prerequisite page; its still-draft item inventory is recorded as a blocker rather than misreported as published.

contents.name: Theorem 4.10, Brauer's First Main Theorem
contents.support: Checks well-definedness, surjectivity, injectivity, normalizer convention, and equality of defect groups.

contents.name: Lecture 3 Min–Max theorem
contents.reason: The notes state rather than prove the key block form used later, so this scaffold uses the independently complete bimodule/Green proof and does not import Min–Max as a hidden premise.

contents.name: Brauer's Second and Third Main Theorems
contents.reason: These character-theoretic refinements belong to the separately planned later Brauer-main-theorem page.

sources.title: David A. Craven, The Brauer Correspondence
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.1–1.3, printed pp. 1–11, and §1.6, printed pp. 13–16.
sources.reading_status: The complete indicated preliminaries, class-localization proof, First Main Theorem proof, and S7 example were inspected. The later conjectural character placement in the example was explicitly excluded.

contents.name: Lemma 1.3, localization of conjugacy classes
contents.support: Independent verification of the class-sum localization behind the central-character comparison.

contents.name: Definition of block induction and defect control
contents.support: Checks the direction of defect containment and definedness convention.

contents.name: Theorem 1.12, Brauer's First Main Theorem
contents.support: Independent central-character proof and definition of the correspondent.

contents.name: Existence half of Theorem 1.12
contents.support: Checks maximal defect and normalizer hypotheses against the selected Green proof.

contents.name: Uniqueness half of Theorem 1.12
contents.support: Checks that distinct local defect-D blocks cannot induce to the same global block.

contents.name: Brauer correspondent terminology
contents.support: Supports introducing the name only after existence and uniqueness.

contents.name: S7 in characteristic 2
contents.support: Supplies the D8 normalizer and local/global block data.

contents.name: Conjectural assignment of individual ordinary characters in the S7 example
contents.reason: The source labels this placement conjectural; the example uses only proved block and defect data and makes no assertion about those individual characters.

contents.name: Extended First Main Theorem and Third Main Theorem material
contents.reason: The assigned pair stops at First Main and block/Green compatibility; later character correspondences require their separately planned page.

sources.title: James P. Saunders, Modular Representation Theory
sources.locator: §5, printed pp. 40–45, including Definitions 5.13, Lemma 5.14, Example 5.15, Theorems 5.16–5.17 and Corollaries 5.18–5.19; Examples 4.31 and 5.5 for SL2(Fp).
sources.reading_status: The entire listed section and referenced examples were inspected, including the Mackey calculations and Green-correspondence proof.

contents.name: Definition 5.13, block induction
contents.support: Primary bimodule definition used in the manifest.

contents.name: Lemma 5.14(i), defect control
contents.support: Complete diagonal-vertex proof.

contents.name: Lemma 5.14(ii), transitivity
contents.support: Complete restriction/uniqueness proof.

contents.name: Lemma 5.14(iii), centralizer-containment existence
contents.support: Complete Mackey double-coset proof.

contents.name: Example 5.15, condition not necessary
contents.support: Odd dihedral normal-complement counterexample, including n=3.

contents.name: Theorem 5.16, First Main Theorem
contents.support: Complete Green-correspondence proof of both directions and uniqueness.

contents.name: Theorem 5.16, local existence
contents.support: Green correspondent of the diagonal block bimodule supplies the local block.

contents.name: Theorem 5.16, local-to-global direction
contents.support: A local block of diagonal vertex ΔD has a unique global Green correspondent.

contents.name: Theorem 5.16, corresponding block bimodules
contents.support: Identifies the two block ideals as the distinguished Green pair.

contents.name: Theorem 5.17 and Corollary 5.18, block compatibility
contents.support: Supports the statement; Farrell–Lassueur supplies the complete proof inspected for this scaffold.

contents.name: Corollary 5.19, full-defect vertex module
contents.support: Projective-cover and Green-correspondence construction.

contents.name: Examples 4.31 and 5.5, SL2(Fp)
contents.support: Explicit restriction, head, parity-block, and Steinberg data.

contents.name: Cyclic-defect Brauer trees and later main-theorem material
contents.reason: Those results require cyclic-block and character-theoretic machinery beyond this pair's First Main and block-compatibility scope.

sources.locator: Complete chapter, pp. 1–13; specifically Definition 40.1, Proposition 40.3, Theorems 40.4–40.5 and Corollary 40.7.
sources.reading_status: The full chapter and all relevant proofs were inspected, including every Mackey/double-coset step in Theorem 40.5 and the projective-cover proof of Corollary 40.7.

contents.name: Definition 40.1, block induction
contents.support: Independent bimodule formulation.

contents.name: Remark 40.2, double-coset exclusion
contents.support: The proper-vertex exclusion used in the direct compatibility proof.

contents.name: Proposition 40.3(i), defect control
contents.support: Second complete proof of diagonal-vertex containment.

contents.name: Proposition 40.3(ii), transitivity
contents.support: Second complete proof of defined-expression transitivity.

contents.name: Proposition 40.3(iii), centralizer containment
contents.support: Second complete existence and uniqueness proof.

contents.name: Theorem 40.4, Brauer's First Main Theorem
contents.support: Complete independent Green-correspondence proof.

contents.name: Theorem 40.4, injective distinguished summand
contents.support: Uniqueness of the local block summand.

contents.name: Theorem 40.5, block compatibility
contents.support: Complete direct proof avoiding any later Nagao decomposition dependency.

contents.name: Corollary 40.7, full-defect vertex
contents.support: Independent projective-cover/Green proof; the scaffold corrects the source's evident final-module ambient-group typo.

contents.name: Corollary 40.8, defect-zero characterization
